feedback.problem:
The triangle $D$ has vertices $(1,1),(5,1),(3,4).$ What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

$\text{Area}(T(D))=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039564/assets/3e2c56766f201095bee0eea101b877e30910c676c998f37d261fd7cf7aabb837.png)

Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 3=6.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=(-2)\cdot 1-4\cdot 1=-6.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,-6\,|\cdot 6 \\  & =36.\end{aligned}
$$
